BM.name: Blueprint CoC, Monolith and Spell Tower

HD.name: Base Drop, Dragon Rider and Hydra

AQ.name: AllClash, Queen Charge and Hog Riders

NB.name: Clash Ninja, unlocking the sixth builder

heroes.role: Long range damage. Fragile, so she needs healing or protection on a long walk.
heroes.split: Guides split by plan. Unicorn is the pick for Queen Charge, while TH18 war armies mostly run Frosty. GameRant and one TH18 army use Sneezy, but Clash Ninja warns it exposes her to Air Defenses.

picks.why: Heals her through a long Queen Charge.
Slows the defences shooting at her.
Clash Ninja calls it a powerful combination: it breaks the walls that would block her.
A backup that survives one big burst.

avoid.why: Her range is longer than its 4.5 tiles, so it runs ahead of her (Clash Ninja).

heroes.role: Support. His ability protects the army from big hits, and he can walk or fly over walls.
heroes.split: Sneezy leads at TH17 and up. AllClash still prefers Electro Owl in air mode and Poison Lizard in ground mode.

picks.why: Boogers soak up hits meant for him. Clash Ninja says air mode only.
Long range suits air mode. The usual pick below TH17.
The usual pick for ground mode.
Strong for Warden Walks and Fireball.
Stays protected behind the troops.

avoid.why: He's rarely in danger, so its revive is mostly wasted (Clash Ninja).
His range is longer than its 4.5 tiles (Clash Ninja).

heroes.role: Dives over walls and hits defences alone, so staying alive decides how far she gets.
heroes.split: The most disputed hero. AllClash calls Diggy the best pairing in the game, GameRant picks Spirit Fox, Base Drop picks Phoenix, and Clash Ninja backs L.A.S.S.I, Diggy and Spirit Fox.

picks.why: Invisibility lets her dive defences and reset Infernos.
She goes deep alone, so a second life pays off.
Stuns the defences she goes for.
Clash Ninja calls it a strong combination: it can get ahead of her and tank.
Healing, before the better pets unlock.

avoid.why: She already goes for defences, so it adds nothing (Clash Ninja).
It leads her into Air Defenses (Clash Ninja).

heroes.role: Tanky flying hero. He gets stronger when separated from friendly flying units.
heroes.split: Angry Jelly leads for clearing defences. 1337wiki's Duke Charge armies use Spirit Fox.

picks.why: Keeps him attacking defences.
Invisibility on a Duke Charge.
Extra survival.
Hangs back, so defences rarely target it.

avoid.why: AllClash and Clash Ninja both say its Boogers stop his enrage.
A ground pet can't keep up with a flying hero. Clash Ninja says the same of Unicorn and Frosty.

heroes.role: Tough melee tank. Good for taking down a corner and making a funnel.
heroes.split: Most guides favour Frosty or Phoenix. Base Drop picks Spirit Fox first instead.

picks.why: Slows the defences wearing him down.
A second chance to finish a compartment.
Invisibility through the first ring of defences.
Clears defences early on.
Opens walls and compartments up close.

avoid.why: It runs ahead and dies (Clash Ninja).
His short range leaves it exposed to Air Defenses (Clash Ninja).
It gets exposed to Air Defenses (Clash Ninja).

heroes.role: Flying damage dealer that can stay with an air army.
heroes.split: AllClash and GameRant pick Angry Jelly. Base Drop picks Electro Owl, and Clash Ninja rates both.

picks.why: Lets him charge with an air army and clear defences.
A fallback for survival.
Matches his ranged attack. The pick before Angry Jelly unlocks.
Stuns defences while it digs.

avoid.why: Close range, and a poor fit for a flying hero (Clash Ninja).

pets.L.A.S.S.I: Best on the Royal Champion, where it can get ahead and tank. On the King it runs ahead and dies.
pets.Electro Owl: Long range support. The early favourite for the Warden.
pets.Mighty Yak: Opens compartments for a King going in close.
pets.Unicorn: Healing. The classic Queen Charge partner.
pets.Frosty: Slows defences. A popular all-round war pet.
pets.Diggy: Rated very differently between guides. Strongest with the Royal Champion.
pets.Poison Lizard: Fast and slows defences. Suits a ground mode Warden.
pets.Phoenix: Saves a hero from one big hit. Best on heroes that dive alone.
pets.Spirit Fox: Invisibility on a hero that needs to get deep.
pets.Angry Jelly: Turns the hero onto defences. Top pick for Dragon Duke and Minion Prince.
pets.Sneezy: Boogers take hits for the hero. Best on a Warden in air mode. Avoid on the King, Queen and Dragon Duke.
pets.Greedy Raven: A farming pet that hits resource buildings. Swap it out for war, unless your plan needs its storage damage.

townHalls.summary: Tanks in front, damage behind, and your first Wall Breakers.

strategies.name: Giants and Archers
strategies.about: Giants soak up the hits while Archers do the damage. Wall Breakers open a way in.
steps: Send Giants first, at the defences.
Use Wall Breakers to reach the Mortar early.
Spread Archers behind the Giants, and use the last ones to clean up.

townHalls.summary: Balloons are strong while anti-air is thin.

strategies.name: Balloons and Archers
strategies.about: Balloons go straight for defences, and most bases here have little to stop them.
steps: Clear the Air Defense and Archer Towers first, as they are the Balloons' main threat.
Send the Balloons together.
Finish with Archers.

townHalls.summary: Mix ground and air, and start using spells.

strategies.name: Giants, Wizards and Balloons
strategies.about: A ground push takes out the Air Defense, then Balloons finish from the other side.
steps: Push Giants and Wizards towards the Air Defense.
Break walls with Wall Breakers.
Send Balloons from the opposite side once it falls.

townHalls.summary: Air gets harder with more Air Defenses and the Air Sweeper, so go by ground.

strategies.name: Giant and Wizard push
strategies.about: A full ground push with Healing Spells. Skycoach warns that air is inconsistent at this level.
steps: Lead with Giants.
Follow with Wizards and open walls with Wall Breakers.
Drop Healing Spells on the push when it comes under fire.

townHalls.summary: Dragons arrive, and they are the safest three-star for several Town Halls.

strategies.name: Mass Dragons
strategies.about: The most forgiving war army at this level. Air Defenses are still few and weak.
steps: Snipe an Air Defense with Lightning first.
Deploy from behind the Air Sweeper, in a spread line.
Rage the Dragons when they reach the core.

strategies.name: Mass Hog Riders
strategies.about: A ground option that jumps walls. Traps matter more than with Dragons.
steps: Pull out or clear Clan Castle troops first.
Send Hog Riders together.
Heal them where splash and traps hit.

townHalls.summary: Time ground attacks with the Queen, or stay on Dragons.

strategies.name: Mass Dragons
strategies.about: Still a strong beginner army here, and it needs no new skills.
steps: Take out an Air Defense with Lightning.
Deploy in a spread line.
Rage the core.

strategies.name: GoHo
strategies.about: Golems, Hog Riders and Wizards. Teaches timing and spell placement.
steps: Golem tanks one side while Wizards clear a funnel.
Send Hog Riders through the gap.
Heal the Hogs where defences overlap.

strategies.name: Golem and Valkyrie push
strategies.about: A structured ground push that pays off against strong cores.
steps: Golems take the hits.
Open the core with Wall Breakers.
Send Valkyries in, with Rage on arrival.

townHalls.summary: Witches reward steady pressure, and Lava Hounds open up air.

strategies.name: Witch Slap
strategies.about: Golems in front and Witches behind. It wins by pressure more than precision.
steps: Golems first, to take the fire.
Open a path with Wall Breakers or Jump.
Deploy Witches behind them, then Rage, Freeze and Heal as needed.

strategies.name: Zap Dragons
strategies.about: Spells clear the Air Defenses, then the Dragons have an easy run.
steps: Earthquake and Lightning an Air Defense.
Use heroes on the remaining Air Defenses.
Deploy the Dragons.

strategies.name: Zap Lalo
strategies.about: Lava Hounds tank for Balloons. Strong, but needs precise timing.
steps: Zap an Air Defense with Lightning.
Send the King and Queen at high-value defences.
Lava Hounds first, Balloons close behind.

townHalls.summary: Inferno Towers arrive. Zap Dragons stays simple, and Queen Charge starts here.

strategies.name: Zap Dragons
strategies.about: Remove the Air Defenses before the Dragons deploy. Low risk.
steps: Lightning and Earthquake the Air Defenses.
Use the Queen and Prince on what remains.
Deploy the Dragons.

strategies.name: Queen Charge Hybrid
strategies.about: The Queen with Healers clears one side, then Hog Riders and Miners finish. It adapts to most bases.
steps: Walk the Queen with her Healers, keeping her clear of single-target Inferno Towers.
Use Healing Spells to keep her alive.
Send Hog Riders and Miners together once the path is clear.

strategies.name: Zap Lalo
strategies.about: A classic air three-star for players who already know their timing.
steps: Zap Air Defenses with Lightning.
Send Lava Hounds first.
Balloons behind them, with Haste and Heal.

townHalls.summary: Zap Witches is the easy three-star. The Warden and Eagle Artillery change planning.

strategies.name: Zap Witches
strategies.about: Very forgiving. Spells take out the Inferno Towers, then Witches walk through.
steps: Lightning and Earthquake the Inferno Towers.
Make a wide funnel.
Send Golems, then Witches and heroes through the centre. Use the Warden's ability when the push takes heavy damage.

strategies.name: Electro Dragons
strategies.about: One of the easier air armies. Chain lightning works best in a straight line.
steps: Funnel with heroes or one Electro Dragon.
Send the rest in a straight line, with Balloons on the defences in their way.
Rage and Freeze along the path.

strategies.name: Queen Charge Hybrid
strategies.about: The versatile option for skilled players. Higher reward, less forgiving.
steps: Queen and Healers clear one side.
Use Healing Spells and the Warden's ability to keep her alive.
Send Hog Riders and Miners to finish.

townHalls.summary: Siege machines arrive and make air attacks more controlled.

strategies.name: Zap Dragons
strategies.about: Simple and reliable, and it doesn't need epic equipment.
steps: Use Giant Arrow, Lightning and Earthquake on the Air Defenses.
Funnel with the King.
Deploy the Dragons, with a Battle Blimp on the core. Rage and Freeze when needed.

strategies.name: Yeti Smash
strategies.about: A ground alternative. Yetis and their Yetimites overwhelm the defences behind a tank.
steps: Make a funnel with heroes.
Send the Yetis behind an Ice Golem, which takes the hits.
Rage and Freeze as they reach the core.

strategies.name: DragBat
strategies.about: Dragons weaken the splash defences, then Bat Spells swarm what's left. Timing decides it.
steps: Deploy Dragons with a Battle Blimp or Stone Slammer.
Wait until splash defences are gone.
Drop Bat Spells outside them, and Freeze what still threatens the Bats.

strategies.name: Queen Charge Hybrid
strategies.about: Still strong here if you can control the charge.
steps: Queen and Healers clear one side.
Heal her, and save the Warden's ability for big hits.
Send Hog Riders and Miners to finish.

townHalls.summary: The Royal Champion arrives, and Yetis are the ground answer.

strategies.name: Yeti Super Archer Spam
strategies.about: Simple to deploy, with a lot of forgiving damage.
steps: Ice Golems and heroes open the attack.
Send Yetis and a Log Launcher.
Super Archers behind them, Rage on the core.

strategies.name: Yeti and Super Wizard Smash
strategies.about: A heavy ground push. Keep the heroes grouped under the Warden's ability.
steps: Open a side with heroes and a Log Launcher.
Send Yetis then Super Wizards.
Use the Warden's ability when the group is under fire.

strategies.name: Super Archer Clone Hydra
strategies.about: One of the most reliable air attacks, but with several moving parts.
steps: Fly Super Archers in on a Battle Blimp, with Invisibility and Clone.
Send the Royal Champion at the back of the base.
Follow with a Lava Hound, Dragons, Balloons and Dragon Riders.

townHalls.summary: The Pet House opens. Most guides pick a Dragon army here.

strategies.name: Super Dragons
strategies.about: One of the most reliable armies here, and forgiving to deploy.
steps: Take out an Air Defense with the Queen or spells.
Deploy Super Dragons along one side.
Balloons on defences in the way, then Rage and Freeze.

strategies.name: Mass Dragons with Blimp
strategies.about: The Queen's Giant Arrow handles an Air Defense, and the Blimp goes for the Town Hall.
steps: Giant Arrow on an Air Defense.
Send the Battle Blimp towards the Town Hall.
Deploy Dragons with Balloons, then Rage and Freeze.

strategies.name: RC Walk Dragons
strategies.about: Very strong once the Champion's walk has cleared key defences.
steps: Walk the Royal Champion through defences with Rocket Spear, using Invisibility to keep her alive.
Clear Air Defenses with Rocket Balloons.
Deploy the Dragons.

townHalls.summary: Root Riders and Dragon Duke arrive, and ground smash takes over.

strategies.name: Root Rider with RC Charge
strategies.about: Trophy Coach calls it the most consistent high Town Hall ground army of 2026, and the default when unsure.
steps: Charge the Royal Champion along one side.
Root Riders push through defences and walls.
Overgrowth keeps defences busy while the push gets through.

strategies.name: Warden Charge Super Yetis
strategies.about: The Warden leads with Healers, and Super Yetis push behind him.
steps: Open with the Warden and Healers.
Use Furnaces and Skeleton Spells to pull fire.
Send Super Yetis in behind, with Jump where walls block them.

strategies.name: Hydra
strategies.about: A triple air mix where pathing decides everything. Avoid the Clan Castle.
steps: Plan the path around the Clan Castle.
Drop Clone Spells where the Battle Blimp releases its troops.
Deploy Dragons, Dragon Riders and Balloons.

townHalls.note: Picked before Town Hall 19, which Supercell says lands in mid-November 2026. Expect these to change.
townHalls.summary: Merged defences arrive. Super Yetis and Root Riders lead.

strategies.name: Fireball Super Yeti
strategies.about: Blueprint CoC calls it safe and consistent, and Trophy Coach the most forgiving high Town Hall three-star.
steps: Soften defences with the Warden's Fireball.
Send Super Yetis with the King and Royal Champion.
Totem, Jump and Rage to carry the push into the core.

strategies.name: RC Walk Root Riders
strategies.about: Strong, but needs precise control of the Champion's walk.
steps: Walk the Royal Champion with Invisibility.
Send Root Riders along the cleared side.
Use Overgrowth and Totems to keep them going.

strategies.name: Root Riders and Valkyries
strategies.about: Controlled ground movement rather than spam.
steps: Clear space with a Siege Barracks.
Send Root Riders first, then Valkyries and Super Barbarians.
Use Overgrowth and Rage to control the path.

strategies.name: RC Walk Dragons
strategies.about: Fast and explosive when the walk takes out the right targets.
steps: Walk the Royal Champion with Invisibility.
Deploy Dragons on the opened side.
Clean up the rest.

townHalls.note: Picked before Town Hall 19, which Supercell says lands in mid-November 2026. Expect these to change.
townHalls.summary: Sneezy, Meteor Golem and the Firespitter. Precise entries matter more.

strategies.name: Fireball Super Yetis
strategies.about: Blueprint CoC calls it one of the most consistent smash attacks here.
steps: Use the Warden's Fireball, Invisibility and Earthquake to open the way in.
Ice Golems take the hits.
Send Super Yetis, with Jump into the core.

strategies.name: RC Walk Dragons
strategies.about: Extremely strong when the walk works. Invisibility is used on the spot to steer the Dragons' path.
steps: Walk the Royal Champion with Invisibility.
Clear defences with Rocket Balloons and a Siege Barracks.
Deploy Dragons, using Invisibility to steer them.

strategies.name: RC Walk Root Riders
strategies.about: Blueprint CoC calls it one of the strongest ground strategies here.
steps: Walk the Royal Champion with Invisibility.
Use a Troop Launcher to get support to her.
Send Root Riders with Overgrowth.

strategies.name: Hydra Air
strategies.about: A two-flank air attack that needs Air Defenses you can split.
steps: Check the Air Defenses can be split into two flanks.
Open with a Lava Hound and Balloons.
Send Dragons and Dragon Riders, with Rage, Freeze and Poison.

townHalls.note: Picked before Town Hall 19, which Supercell says lands in mid-November 2026. Expect these to change.
townHalls.summary: Supercell's July war data had Dragon armies and Throwers with Healers at about 40% of TH18 attacks between them.

strategies.name: Super Yeti with RC Charge
strategies.about: The most forgiving high Town Hall three-star, according to Trophy Coach.
steps: Soften defences with Fireball or a Log Launcher.
Send a tank and Super Yetis.
Charge the Royal Champion behind them with Electro Boots.

strategies.name: Root Rider Yeti
strategies.about: Root Riders push defences and Super Yetis push the core. High health troops are at risk from the Monolith, so plan to remove it early.
steps: The King and Giants make the funnel.
The Royal Champion pushes one side.
Send Root Riders, then Super Yetis into the core.

strategies.name: Dragon Duke Charge Hydra
strategies.about: From the most used army type in Supercell's July data. Fire Heart was nerfed in October, so older hit rates may flatter it.
steps: Charge the Dragon Duke along one side, using Invisibility.
Send Inferno Dragons, a Lava Hound and Rocket Balloons.
Dragon Riders follow, with Totem, Freeze and Poison.

strategies.name: Rocket Backpack Throwers
strategies.about: Throwers backed by Healers were the second most used army type in Supercell's July data.
steps: Open with the Dragon Duke on Rocket Backpack.
Open walls with Wall Breakers and clear the way with Lightning.
Send Throwers and Healers, with Totem, Overgrowth and Freeze.

strategies.name: Ruin Witch
strategies.about: Supercell put Ruin Witch attacks at about 76% three-stars, against a 53% average, before an October nerf to her Ruin Knights. Those figures may now flatter her.
steps: Make a funnel for them.
Deploy the Ruin Witches, which summon Ruin Knights.
Support the push with Rage and Freeze.

Barbarian.role: Cheap filler for funnels, clean-up and taking the first shots.
use: Drop a few at the edge first to draw fire and set off traps.
Use them to clear outside buildings so stronger troops walk inwards.
beware: Splash from Mortars and Wizard Towers kills a clump, so spread them out.
Too weak to carry an attack past the low Town Halls.

Archer.role: Cheap ranged damage that shoots over walls.
use: Spread them behind a tank, so defences are shooting something else.
A thin line clears outside buildings quickly.
beware: Very little health. Splash wipes a clump, so never drop them in one spot.

Goblin.role: Farming troop that goes for resources before anything else.
use: Send them once something else is drawing fire near the storages.
Pick them for loot raids, not for stars.
beware: They ignore the defences shooting them, and have little health.

Giant.role: Low Town Hall tank that walks to the nearest defence.
use: Drop them first, then damage troops once defences have locked on.
Open a wall for them, or they lose time hitting it.
A Healer behind a group keeps them going much longer.
beware: Low damage, so they stall without support.
Golems and Yetis replace them as tanks from about TH8. After that they are mainly funnel troops.

Wall Breaker.role: Opens walls, so ground troops reach the defences instead of stalling.
use: Send them just after your tank, while defences are looking elsewhere.
Send small groups, so one trap or Mortar shot does not lose them all.
Aim for the wall of the compartment you want to enter.
beware: They die to almost anything, and Spring Traps can throw them away.
Sent too early, they die before they reach the wall.

Balloon.role: Slow flying bomber that goes for defences and hits hard.
use: Send them behind a Lava Hound, which soaks up the Air Defense fire.
Haste keeps them moving through Air Defense range.
Send them together from one side, so they arrive as a group.
beware: Air Defenses, Seeking Air Mines and Scattershots are what stop them.
They cannot hit air troops, and are slow without Haste.

Wizard.role: Fragile splash damage that hits ground and air.
use: Keep them behind a tank, spread in a line.
Good at clearing groups of buildings and enemy swarms.
beware: Very little health once the tank has gone.

Healer.role: Keeps ground troops and heroes alive. Does no damage.
use: Pair with troops that bunch up, as one Healer can then cover several.
Deal with Air Defenses on the route first, or plan a path around them.
A Queen Walk or Thrower pack is the classic use.
beware: Air Defenses and Seeking Air Mines kill them, and the army collapses after that.
They cannot heal air units or Siege Machines. Too many on one target is wasted.

Dragon.role: Tough flying splash damage. The main army at TH7, and still used well above it.
use: Remove or weaken Air Defenses first with Lightning.
Make a funnel so they walk into the core, not around the edge.
Save Rage for the core.
beware: Air Defenses plus Seeking Air Mines, especially at higher Town Halls without a Lightning plan.
Without a funnel they drift round the outside and time runs out.

P.E.K.K.A.role: Big melee damage and health in one body.
use: Send behind a Golem with Wizards and Wall Breakers.
Point it at the part of the base with the toughest buildings.
beware: Single target, so Skeleton Traps and swarms waste its time.
Multi-target Infernos split its focus and hurt.
Under 3% of TH18 war attacks in Supercell's October figures, before its damage buff.

Baby Dragon.role: Flying splash that gets much stronger when no other air unit is near.
use: Use one or two apart from your air group to clear the outside for a funnel.
Send it where it can work alone, as its bonus needs that.
beware: Nearby air troops switch off its bonus damage and attack speed.

Miner.role: Tunnels under walls, and comes up right beside each target.
use: Walls do not slow them, so they suit heavily walled bases.
Healing Spells and Healers keep the group going when they surface.
They still get spell bonuses underground.
beware: They only take damage when above ground, but hit one target at a time.
Ice Block does not protect them while they are underground.
Under 3% of TH18 war attacks in Supercell's October figures, before their health buff.

Yeti.role: Heavy ground hitter, whose Yetimites come out as it takes damage.
use: Make a funnel first, then send them in a group to smash through.
A Log Launcher ahead of them opens the way.
Save Rage for when they reach the core.
beware: Multi-target Infernos cut through the swarm.
Slow, so a late start can run out of time.

Electro Dragon.role: Slow flying lightning that chains between close buildings.
use: Use Lightning on Air Defenses before you send them.
A group can clear a compartment quickly when buildings sit close together.
It strikes the ground when destroyed, so one lost deep still does damage.
beware: Very slow, so a long walk can run out the clock.
Chains do less on spread-out bases.

Dragon Rider.role: Flying heavy hitter that goes straight for defences.
use: Open with a hero or tank so it reaches defences while they are distracted.
Totem and Freeze buy time when it gets into the core.
beware: Air Defenses and Seeking Air Mines, as with every air army.
It leaves other buildings standing, so plan who cleans up.

Electro Titan.role: Walking tank with an aura that damages everything around her.
use: Drop one on a flank to help make the funnel.
Walk her with the main group, so her aura and health both help.
beware: Short range, so she walks right into defences and takes the hits.

Root Rider.role: Ground bruiser that smashes walls and goes for defences.
use: Send a group of five to seven to open a walled base for the rest of the army.
Overgrowth on the defensive core stops them stalling there.
Save Rage for the core and Freeze for the defence melting them.
beware: The Monolith hits high health troops hardest, so plan to remove it early.

Thrower.role: Long range damage that hits ground and air, from outside many defences.
use: Clear the outside on both shoulders first, so they walk into the core. A hero or two Root Riders each side does it.
Keep the pack bunched so Healers can cover it. About four Healers is usual.
Freeze the splash defences, and Rage a pack that has stalled.
beware: Without a funnel they wander the edge and shoot storages.
Air Defenses ignore them but kill the Healers, which collapses the attack.
Scattershots and multi-target Infernos punish the bunch.

Meteor Golem.role: Tank that splits into two Meteormites on each throw, then re-forms.
use: Start with a couple up front, and keep them close so the halves can recombine.
Use a hero or side troops to set the entry point.
Pair with a damage carry, as it is not a solo army.
beware: Spread too thin, the halves die alone and never re-form.
Only Meteormites cross walls, not a whole Golem. Cloned ones cannot merge.

use: Use them to clean up edges or fill spare housing in an air army.
Seeking Air Mines ignore them, so they can go ahead of others.
beware: Very fragile. Air Sweepers and splash make short work of a group.

Hog Rider.role: Fast ground troop that jumps walls and goes for defences.
use: Kill the Clan Castle and make a funnel first, or the group scatters.
Heal them ahead of where they are going, not where they stand.
Keep a Freeze for the Inferno Tower that locks on.
beware: Two Giant Bombs together can wipe out a group.
Infernos burn the group unless they are Frozen.
Under 3% of TH18 war attacks in Supercell's October figures, before their health buff.

Valkyrie.role: Melee spinner that shreds groups of buildings and troops at once.
use: Best where buildings sit tightly together, usually the core.
Send them behind a tank through an open funnel.
Rage on a group inside the core is the payoff.
beware: Walls cost her a lot of time, so have an entry ready.

Golem.role: The main tank at middle Town Halls. Walks to defences and soaks up fire.
use: Drop first and let defences lock on, especially Inferno Towers.
Follow with Wall Breakers, then your damage troops.
Golemites still draw fire after it falls, so give them time to work.
beware: Very little damage, so it needs an army behind it.
Super Witches and Yetis largely replace it higher up.

Witch.role: Support that keeps raising Skeletons to soak up shots.
use: Keep her behind a tank, and let the Skeletons distract the defences.
They overload splash and waste single-target defences.
Mass Witches are a common TH9 plan.
beware: Each Skeleton is weak, so she is not a main damage dealer.
Slow and fragile if the front line falls.

Lava Hound.role: Flying tank that goes for Air Defenses and soaks up their fire.
use: Send it first, from the side of the Air Defense you want to tie up.
Air troops follow once it has taken the Air Defense's attention.
When it dies, the Lava Pups keep drawing fire for a moment.
beware: It does almost no damage, so it needs air troops behind it.

Bowler.role: Ranged ground splash whose boulders bounce into whatever is behind.
use: Send them behind a tank, and let the bounce hit two buildings at once.
They work well where buildings are packed together.
beware: Slow, and they cannot hit air troops, so enemy air units need another answer.

Ice Golem.role: Tank that goes for defences, then freezes the area when destroyed.
use: Send one to soak up fire ahead of a push or a Siege Machine.
Let it die among defences, so the freeze stops them shooting your main group.
beware: Low damage, so it only sets things up.
A freeze far away from your army helps nobody.

Headhunter.role: Goes straight for enemy heroes, jumps walls, and slows them with poison.
use: Drop her close to a defending hero, so she gets there quickly.
Removing a hero early protects your main push.
beware: Little use once the enemy heroes are gone.
She will not clear a route, as she ignores other targets while a hero is up.

Apprentice Warden.role: Ground support whose aura gives nearby troops extra health.
use: Walk him with tough troops, so the aura covers as many as possible.
Drop him behind the front so he reaches the middle of the group.
beware: No Eternal Tome, so he only adds health, not protection from big hits.
Siege Machines get nothing from the aura.

Druid.role: Heals several troops at once, then turns into a Bear as a fighter.
use: Send with heroes on a dive for quick healing.
Works in Yeti smash and Super Witch armies.
beware: Bears get stuck behind walls, so Druids struggle on heavily walled bases.

Furnace.role: Sits still and sends Firemites at buildings over its lifetime.
use: Place it out of range of defences, by the outside buildings you want gone.
Use it to open up a base so the rest of the army gets deeper.
beware: Destroyed early, its remaining Firemites are lost.
Launch guides say healing it to full stops the Firemites, so keep Healers away from it.

Ruin Witch.role: Support that turns rubble into Ruin Knights. Top three-star rate of any troop with real use in Supercell's October TH18 war figures.
use: Drop her behind the front line once the first buildings have fallen.
Keep her close to the main push, so Knights appear where they are needed.
One is usually enough, unless the army is built around her.
beware: Dropped too early she stands idle, and near defences she dies before making Knights.
She cannot jump walls, so the funnel must be open.
Spring Traps can throw Knights since October. Compact bases clump them for splash.

use: Use them to clear the outside and open a funnel for the main army.
beware: Few high-end armies use them for much else.
They die quickly to splash when bunched.

Super Archer.role: Arrows pierce through buildings and reach targets several buildings away.
use: Drop them in a Battle Blimp from your Clan Castle, with Invisibility, to remove a key defence.
Use them to make a funnel or clean up, as they reach so far.
They spam well alongside Yetis at TH13.
beware: Clan Castle troops that travel too far while invisible can be shot down.
Eagle Artillery and Scattershots can catch them at TH18.

Super Wall Breaker.role: Rolling bomb that always blows up, so it gets through where normal ones die.
use: Use for wall spots covered by a multi-target Inferno Tower.
Good for opening a chosen section on a Queen Charge.
beware: Plain Wall Breakers are enough most of the time.

Super Giant.role: Very tanky, and punches through walls.
use: Use as a tank in a push, with Healers behind.
beware: Slow with low damage, so hard to justify the boost at higher Town Halls.
It can break walls in unhelpful spots.

Sneaky Goblin.role: Goblin that stays hidden for a while after being deployed.
use: Pair with a Battle Blimp to take out the Town Hall for a quick star.
Use it for loot on a raid, if you have a boost spare.
beware: Little health once revealed, and not much use beyond those two jobs.

Super Miner.role: Stronger tunnelling Miner with a blast at the end.
use: Keep Healing Spells and Healers ready when the group surfaces.
beware: Rated low in current guides: its tunnelling can be unpredictable, and it is barely picked at TH18.
Base Drop suggests skipping it for CWL. It got a health buff in October, so re-check.

Rocket Balloon.role: Balloon with booster rockets that gets to defences quickly.
use: Send them after a Lava Hound or a hero has drawn the first shots.
The speed gets them in before Air Defenses thin them out.
beware: Scattershots and Seeking Air Mines still punish them.
The boost does not last the whole attack, so they slow to Balloon pace.

Inferno Dragon.role: Beam that builds up the longer it stays on one target.
use: Point it at tough buildings, where the beam has time to build.
Used in Duke Charge air armies alongside Dragon Riders.
beware: Poor at clearing lots of small buildings.
AllClash rates it better on defence in a Clan Castle than on attack, though that page is old.

Super Valkyrie.role: Spinning splash with a wider reach, leaving Rage when she falls.
use: Send several, so one falling boosts the others.
Suits spam attacks with no room for your own Rage Spells.
beware: Needs more careful placement than Super Witches.
Rated mid-table by Base Drop, and AllClash avoids her in war.

Super Witch.role: Summons one big tanky Big Boy instead of many Skeletons. Among the most forgiving war troops.
use: Deploy a wide line of about six.
Works best at about TH11 to TH16.
Pair with Root Riders and the Warden, or a few Golems.
beware: Big clusters draw Scattershots, so keep a Freeze for them.
She is slow, so start with plenty of time.

Ice Hound.role: Tanky flyer that freezes the area where it comes down.
use: Use like a Lava Hound, tying up Air Defenses for your flyers.
Time your followers so they arrive as the freeze lands.
beware: Little damage on its own, so it needs air troops behind it.

Super Bowler.role: Slow ground splash with boulders that hit three times.
use: Send a group through a funnel, behind a tank, for big damage on packed buildings.
Save Rage for the core.
beware: Slow, so long routes can run out the clock.
Cannot hit air troops.

Super Dragon.role: Flying fire that destroys clusters of buildings in bursts.
use: Use a mass of them with a funnel, like Mass Dragons.
Rage and Freeze keep the group alive through the core.
beware: Base Drop says it struggles from TH16, where building health is too high.

use: Use to make a funnel or clear a section, often from a Battle Blimp.
Used with Yetis for smash at TH13.
beware: Needs buildings at the right spacing to chain well, so it is niche.
Fragile, so keep a tank in front.

Super Minion.role: Flying long range sniper of defences.
use: Support for air armies, picking off defences from far away.
Also a strong Clan Castle defender.
beware: Too big to slip past Seeking Air Mines, unlike normal Minions.

Super Hog Rider.role: Hog and Rider who split up and keep fighting.
use: Mostly useful as a distraction, or to set off Giant Bombs for what follows.
Better as a Clan Castle defender than a main attacker.
beware: Base Drop calls it underwhelming as a main troop from TH16, and Supercell says it is barely picked at TH18. It got a health buff in October.

Super Yeti.role: Base Drop's top ground Super Troop. Its Yetimites zap nearby buildings when it is hit.
use: Send with a tank in front, then Rage behind the group.
Root Riders open the way and Super Yetis carry the core.
A forgiving plan at high Town Halls, with a Royal Champion charge.
beware: Costly to boost, so check your plan before you pay.
The Monolith hits high health troops hardest at TH18.

Wall Wrecker.role: Drives straight at the Town Hall, smashing walls on the way, then releases your Clan Castle troops.
use: Use to open the base at a chosen spot for a ground army or Queen Charge.
Put a tank or heroes with it, as it draws heavy fire.
beware: Single-target Infernos melt it.
Not for air armies, as Clan Castle air troops can meet Seeking Air Mines.
It cannot be healed, and spells do not affect it.

Battle Blimp.role: Flying delivery. It carries your Clan Castle troops to a spot, and is mainly transport.
use: Use it to remove a key defence with Clan Castle troops, plus Rage where they land.
Send a Balloon or two ahead, to clear Seeking Air Mines.
Invisibility protects the troops it drops, not the Blimp itself.
beware: Thin, so Air Defenses bring it down quickly if it flies too far.
Little damage of its own.

Stone Slammer.role: Flying machine that goes for defences, with splash and a quake effect.
use: Good with defence-targeting troops such as Hogs and Balloons, to clear the outer defences.
Used in LaLoon and Queen Walk setups to open a path.
beware: Short range, and Air Defenses handle it easily.
It has no answer to enemy air troops.

Siege Barracks.role: Lands, releases P.E.K.K.As and Wizards, and then your Clan Castle troops.
use: Use it on a flank to help make a funnel, or to clean up when time is short.
Good when you want a distraction more than a core drop.
beware: It stays on the outside, and you have little control after that.
It cannot tank, and its health keeps falling.

Log Launcher.role: Rolls logs ahead of it that smash walls for ground armies.
use: Place it in front of the walls you want gone, then follow with ground troops.
Put a tank in front, as its health drains fast.
beware: Its health keeps falling, so it dies quickly without help.
Slow, and no use to an air army.

Flame Flinger.role: Lobs fire at defences from very long range.
use: Use it to pick off edge defences from outside their reach, before your main troops go in.
Put a tank in front, as its health drains.
beware: Slow, so it can cost you the clock.
Long range defences and traps can still reach it.

Battle Drill.role: Burrows to the nearest defence, pops up, and stuns it.
use: Use it to take out a chosen defence, by placing it close to that defence.
Plan the line it takes, as it goes for the nearest one.
beware: Short range and single target, so it needs a plan rather than a blind drop.

Troop Launcher.role: Stays where it lands, and fires barrels of troops at your army, including your Clan Castle troops.
use: Drop it with your main push, as barrels go to your troops in the field.
Used on RC Walk Root Riders at TH17.
beware: There are only a few barrels and it has a set lifetime, so do not waste it on a thin attack.

Sky Wagon.role: Flying machine that goes for defences and drops barrels of air troops and your Clan Castle troops.
use: Deploy it behind your air troops, as Clash Ninja suggests.
Suits air and hybrid attacks.
beware: Its wooden body cannot take much damage.
Guides on it are thin, so try it in a friendly challenge first.

Lightning Spell.role: Removes Air Defenses before an air attack.
use: Work out how many it takes to kill an Air Defense, and add an Earthquake to save spells.
Also handy on Clan Castle troops or a lone Wizard Tower.
beware: Small radius, so check where your strikes land.

Healing Spell.role: Keeps a ground push alive through sustained fire.
use: Place it 3 to 4 tiles ahead of the group, so they walk into it.
Best for Hogs, Yetis and Super Witches.
beware: Dropped where troops stand now, they walk straight out of it.

Rage Spell.role: The damage and speed boost that finishes off the core.
use: Drop it as the main push reaches the core or Eagle Artillery.
Save it for a group that is starting to stall.
beware: Wasted at the start of an attack, or on troops already winning.

Jump Spell.role: Lets ground troops walk over a section of wall.
use: Place it where the whole group needs to enter the compartment.
Lets you bring fewer Wall Breakers.
beware: Troops will only use it if their route takes them there, so check your funnel.

Freeze Spell.role: Stops a defence that is about to kill something you need.
use: Cast it the moment a defence locks on to your key unit, not before.
Priorities: Inferno on a hero, Scattershot on a cluster, Eagle Artillery opening, Spell Tower on the army.
beware: A second Freeze on the same defence adds little, so use it elsewhere.

Poison Spell.role: Kills or slows Clan Castle troops. Does nothing to buildings.
use: Lure the Clan Castle first, then Poison it before heroes get into a fight.
They also attack and move slower, so it buys time.
beware: Do not send the Queen at Valkyries or Super Valkyries with no Poison on them. It wastes her ability and Healers.

Earthquake Spell.role: Opens walls and softens tough buildings by a share of their health.
use: Use it mainly to open compartments. Four break any wall, and two can make a gap for Root Riders.
It can soften high-health buildings, such as Eagle Artillery and Infernos, before troops arrive.
beware: Each repeat on the same spot does less.
It only hits ground targets.

Haste Spell.role: Faster movement with no damage boost, for one housing space.
use: Cast it on Balloons as they push past mid-base, to stop them stalling under Air Defenses.
Use it when speed matters more than damage.
beware: No damage boost, so Rage is better once troops are hitting the core.

Clone Spell.role: Makes temporary copies of troops that enter it.
use: Cast it on your mid-base Dragons, or on the troops about to enter the core.
Used in Hydra air armies.
beware: There is a housing limit, so it clones only so many at once. Clones also last a short time.
COC Base Guide says it is less useful at higher Town Halls.

Skeleton Spell.role: Instant distraction anywhere on the map, and does not set off traps.
use: Use it on the Monolith or a single-target defence to waste its shots.
Handy against a Town Hall cluster at the end of an attack.
beware: Skeletons can wander, so results vary.

Bat Spell.role: Instant air clean-up that does not set off traps.
use: Use it to finish a Town Hall cluster, or a group of Mortars and Wizard Towers.
Good follow-up in a Dragon or Yeti army.
beware: Bats die quickly to splash, so aim them at a spot with few air-hitting defences.

Invisibility Spell.role: Hides everything inside it, except walls and Siege Machines.
use: Cast it on a hero as an Inferno starts to burn, or across the route of a charge.
Use it on Clan Castle troops after a Blimp drop, so they reach their target.
beware: Lasts a short time, so troops that travel too far come out exposed.
It does not hide your Blimp or other Siege Machines.

Recall Spell.role: Sends troops, heroes and pets back to your deployment bar, to use again elsewhere.
use: Use it to rescue a push that has gone the wrong way, or to save units from a lethal defence.
Redeploy where your Jump or Healing Spells can help.
beware: It does not heal, so hurt troops come back hurt, and it takes the biggest units first.
Anything left undeployed at the end is lost. Totems cannot be recalled.

Overgrowth Spell.role: Roots buildings: they stop firing, cannot be hit, and your troops ignore them.
use: Drop it on the defensive core, ahead of the push and in the direction of travel.
Centre it on a gap between buildings, to catch more defences.
Ground armies gain most, especially Root Riders.
beware: Do not root the building your army is hitting, or the whole pack reroutes.
Traps, Clan Castle troops and heroes still work inside it.
Weak on spread-out bases and hero charges.

Revive Spell.role: Brings back a fallen hero within its range, with some health.
use: Bring it when a hero has to survive deep in the base, where its job is not done.
Wait until the area around the fallen hero is safer, or they will fall again straight away.
beware: Casting it the moment a hero falls is the usual mistake.
It takes two housing spaces, so it replaces something else.

Ice Block Spell.role: Freezes your own troops, so they take far less damage for a few seconds.
use: Cast it on tanks such as Golems, Lava Hounds or Yetis, once they are drawing fire deep in the base.
Follow with your damage troops while defences are wasting shots.
beware: Frozen troops cannot attack, so a badly timed one costs you damage.
It only catches troops already inside. No Siege Machines, underground troops, or spawned troops such as Skeletons.

Totem Spell.role: Drops a tough totem that stuns defences on landing and takes their fire.
use: Drop it near strong defences or units that threaten your army, then follow up with damage.
Use it on the outside first, to protect troops as they go in.
beware: Stun is brief, and its health falls by itself, so timing matters. It does not set off traps.
It cannot be Cloned, Recalled or protected by Ice Block. Healers and Druids do not go for it.

Angry Spell.role: Makes troops inside it faster, and sends them at defences for a short time.
use: Cast it on troops stuck on outside buildings, to turn them on the defences.
Blueprint pairs it with a Ruin Witch, as buildings fall faster and Knights arrive sooner.
beware: Short lived, so time it for when they reach the defences you care about.
A newer spell with few good guides, so try it in a friendly challenge first.

use: Send him along one side to take out a corner and start the funnel.
Spiky Ball is the usual first pick. Earthquake Boots suit wall-breaking pushes, and Giant Gauntlet suits a tank role.
Use his ability before an Inferno Tower has him locked down, not after.
beware: Melee, so walls and Clan Castle troops stall him.
A single-target Inferno burns him quickly, so keep a Freeze back.

use: Queen Walk or Charge with Healers behind her is the classic plan.
Action Figure is the top pick by most guides, as it works like a second life.
Giant Arrow can take out Air Defenses and Air Sweepers from level 9 up.
beware: Low health. Use Invisibility or Freeze as an Inferno starts to burn her.
Poison enemy Valkyries first, or she wastes her ability and Healers on them.

use: Walk with the main group: on foot for ground armies, flying for air armies.
Eternal Tome is the safest first upgrade, as it protects the army through the worst moment.
Fireball cracks defence clusters on ground smashes. Rage Gem helps a longer fight.
beware: Low health. If he falls early, the army loses its protection.
Fire the Tome on the big hit, not as soon as it is ready.

use: Drop her where she can jump to the first defence straight away.
Electro Boots is the top pick. Seeking Shield hits several defences on a charge, and Rocket Spear snipes one.
She leads RC Walk and RC Charge plans, with Invisibility on the way in.
beware: Short range and alone, so she falls quickly if several defences lock on.
Skeleton Traps slow her down unless she has Electro Boots.

use: Drop him 4 to 5 tiles from the defences you want cleared, not at the map edge.
He flies to the nearest buildings, so placement decides his route.
Dark Orb and Dark Crown are the usual pair. The Orb slows and damages what it touches.
beware: He does not handle Clan Castle troops well, so deal with them first.
Base Drop calls him a specialist, not a main carry, and rates him for CWL clean-up.

use: Send your ground core first, then drop him on a lane no friendly air unit will follow.
Fire Heart is the usual first pick, since Healers cannot heal him. Add Flame Blower for burst, Stun Blaster for control, or Electro Fangs on packed bases.
Rocket Backpack flies him straight through the base centre, so line up the angle first. It sits out traps and Clan Castle.
beware: Friendly flyers near him switch off his rage.
Seeking Air Mines hurt him more since July, so route around them.
He lands exposed after a Rocket Backpack, so have follow-up ready.

use: Send with a hero that can keep up, such as the Royal Champion.
beware: It cannot hit air troops, and can run ahead of slow heroes and die alone.

use: Use it when your hero would otherwise stall at walls.
It suits a King going in close, and Clash Ninja likes it with the Queen.
beware: Ground only.
Its rage comes when the hero falls, which is late to be useful.

use: Good on heroes that need ranged support behind them.
An early favourite for the Warden, before Sneezy opens.
beware: Low health, so it needs its hero in front.

use: Best on long walks, as on a Queen Charge, where steady healing adds up.
beware: Steady healing does not save a hero from one big hit.
TH18 war armies have moved away from it to Frosty.

use: A good all-rounder when defences are the main threat.
Frostmites also help slow defences near the hero.
beware: Slowing is not stopping, so you still need a Freeze for Infernos.

use: Strongest on the Royal Champion, where it surfaces to attack buildings beside her.
beware: Guides rate it very differently, so try it in a friendly challenge.

use: Its poison slows defences for a hero nearby. Works for a ground mode Warden.
beware: Very fast, so it can arrive alone with slower heroes.

use: Pick it for heroes that dive alone into danger.
It starts as an egg, then hatches to make the hero briefly invulnerable when they would fall.
beware: It does nothing until that moment, so you give up steady value from another pet.

use: Best on heroes that need to get deep, such as the Royal Champion and Dragon Duke.
beware: Its range is only 4.5 tiles, so it runs ahead of long range heroes such as the Queen.

use: Pick it when you want your hero on defences rather than chewing outside buildings.
A top pick for the Dragon Duke and Minion Prince.
beware: It changes where your hero goes, so plan the path around that.

use: Boogers target buildings and take hits, so it suits a Warden in air mode.
beware: Boogers near the Dragon Duke can cancel his rage.
Clash Ninja warns it exposes the Queen to Air Defenses.

use: A farming pet. Its extra damage to resource buildings is what you pay for.
beware: Swap it out before war, unless your plan needs storage damage.

Air Defense.role: Heavy single-target anti-air. It cannot touch ground troops at all.
use: Send a Lava Hound first. It flies at Air Defenses and soaks up their shots.
Remove one or two with Lightning plus Earthquake before an air attack. Count your spells first.
Let Giants or a hero clear the outer ones, since they take no fire from it.
beware: A few big flyers. Dragons, Healers and flying heroes all take its full hit.
Small groups of Balloons. Send many at once, as it only hits one target per shot.

Air Sweeper.role: Does no damage. Blasts air troops back, leaving them longer under other defences.
use: Check its facing when scouting, then fly in from the side or behind.
Spread air troops in a wide arc, so one gust cannot push them all.
Haste or Rage gets pushed troops back quicker. Ground troops or Lightning can remove it.
beware: Slow flyers. Balloons and Electro Dragons lose the most time, and Inferno Dragons lose their beam.
Healers on a Queen Walk, which get blown away from her.

Archer Tower.role: Single-target tower that hits air and ground. You will meet it at every Town Hall.
use: Swarm it. Each arrow kills one small troop, so a pack of Archers or Barbarians wins.
Outside towers often fall to one strong troop, such as a Valkyrie or Super Barbarian.
Give it a tank to shoot, so your damage troops survive.
beware: Lone troops and thin groups of Balloons, which get picked off on the way in.
Tanks walking up to a Fast Attack tower. It hits far quicker within 8 tiles.

Bomb Tower.role: Short range ground splash that also explodes when destroyed.
use: Send a Giant or Golem in first, and hold melee troops back until it has gone.
It cannot hit air, so Balloons or Minions can remove an exposed one.
A Grand Warden can hit it from outside its reach.
beware: Melee troops that finish it off. A Freeze does not stop the death blast.
Skeletons and Witches, plus Hog Riders if Giant Bombs sit in a gap beside it.

Builder's Hut.role: Harmless early on. From TH14 it can carry a turret, and its Builder repairs nearby buildings.
use: Below TH14, drop one Barbarian or Archer on a corner hut for cheap percentage.
From TH14, kill huts on your attack side, or catch them in your spells.
Freeze stops repairs. Or damage a harmless building first, as he stays on it until it is full.
beware: Spell plans that leave a defence barely alive. The Builder heals it back up.
You cannot hit the Builder himself. Only spells or killing the hut will stop him.

Cannon.role: Basic single-target gun for ground troops. It can never hit air.
use: Send Balloons or Minions if no anti-air covers it, as it cannot shoot back.
Swarm it with Archers or Barbarians, or let a Giant hold its fire.
beware: Wall Breakers, which it picks off before they reach the wall.
Giants, Hog Riders and Valkyries against Burst mode, though Burst wastes shots on swarms.

Eagle Artillery.role: Base-wide artillery for air and ground, up to TH16. At TH17 it merges into the Town Hall.
use: It sleeps until 200 housing is deployed, and heroes and spells count. Spend that on your funnel first.
Freeze it just before a volley. Freezing in the long pause between volleys wastes the spell.
It can't hit closer than 7 tiles, so troops that reach it are safe from its shells.
beware: Tight clumps and heavy targets. Shells land where the most troop health is packed, often your King.
Slow attacks. Once awake it keeps firing volleys into your main army until destroyed.

Firespitter.role: Very long range flames that only fire inside a fixed cone, and shred big single targets.
use: Check its facing when scouting. Troops outside the cone are not targeted, so come from the side or behind.
A second Firespitter may cover that angle. If you must cross, use Freeze or Overgrowth.
A Skeleton Spell in the cone soaks up bursts, as each new target makes it pause.
beware: Heroes and big troops, plus whatever stands behind them. Healers following a Queen get hit too.
Stacks of air and ground. Stray shots hit both, whichever one it aimed at.

Hidden Tesla.role: Stays hidden until something comes close, then zaps one target, air or ground.
use: Look for empty 2x2 gaps inside walls. From TH7 up, these are often Teslas.
Set them off with one cheap troop, instead of walking your army in.
They are thin and short range, so a Giant with Archers or a Grand Warden kills them.
beware: Clusters of gaps, or a Tesla farm. It melts anything you keep feeding into its range.
Hog Riders and Balloons turn towards a revealed Tesla, and can leave your planned path.

Inferno Tower.role: Two modes. Single-target burns hotter the longer it holds, multi-target melts several troops at once.
use: Check its mode when you scout, as the tower looks different in each.
Single-target: Freeze it as it heats up, which resets the beam, or keep it busy with a swarm.
Multi-target: its damage stays fixed, so Healing Spells, Healers and several tanks can outlast it.
beware: Single-target: one tank or hero left under a fully heated beam.
Multi-target: swarms and small troops, such as Yetimites and Skeletons.

Monolith.role: Slow single shots with bonus damage based on the target's maximum health. Built to kill big units.
use: Freeze or Overgrowth stops it. Save one for when your key hero or tank comes into range.
Give it cheap targets. Skeleton, Bat or Totem Spells soak up its slow shots.
Expect a few shots on the first hero to arrive, so do not send a hurt one.
beware: Heroes, Golems, Super Witches and anything else with lots of maximum health.
It hits one target, so spreading out does not save a tank. Cheap targets do.

Mortar.role: Slow long range splash for ground troops. One shell can wipe out a clump.
use: Spread Archers, Barbarians and Goblins out. Never drop them in one spot.
Send Giants first, so shells land on something tough. Fast troops often outrun the shell.
It cannot hit air, or troops right beside it. So fly, or get close.
beware: Clumps of small ground troops, and slow groups that stay in its range.
A geared-up Mortar fires shells in quick runs, so one clump can take several.

Multi-Archer Tower.role: Merged tower that fires three arrows at up to three targets, air or ground.
use: Do not send a hero in alone. Puppets or a group of small troops spread the arrows.
Swarms still work, as three arrows cannot keep up with a big pack.
Time a Freeze for when your main damage arrives. Air armies should remove it early.
beware: Lone targets. With one troop in range, all three arrows hit it.
Lava Pups, as the arrows spread on to them once a Hound pops.

Multi-Gear Tower.role: Merged tower with two modes. Both hit one target at a time, air or ground.
use: Long Range fires slowly at up to 12 tiles, so swarms of small troops waste its shots.
Fast Attack reaches only 8 tiles. Freeze it as tanks arrive, or hit it from further out.
It is thin for its level. Earthquake plus Lightning can remove it before the army arrives.
beware: Fast Attack: tanks and heroes that walk up to it unsupported.
Long Range: single big troops, which it starts hitting well before they get close.

Revenge Tower.role: Starts silent, then wakes and gets faster and deadlier as your attack destroys buildings.
use: It wakes once a few buildings fall. Deal with it early, before it reaches its later stages.
Freeze stops it. Totem and Ice Block soak up its shots.
Overgrowth only pauses it, as it keeps counting fallen buildings while rooted.
beware: Slow, deep attacks. Late on it fires quickly, and shots bounce on to nearby troops.
Clean-up troops at the end of an attack, as bounces hit air and ground alike.

Ricochet Cannon.role: Merged ground-only cannon whose shot bounces on to a second ground troop nearby.
use: Go air. Balloons or Dragons can destroy it without it firing a shot at them.
Spread ground troops, as the bounce only reaches 3.5 tiles.
Freeze it as tanks arrive, which stops both shots while damage troops close in.
beware: Tight ground pushes, above all damage troops right behind a tank.
A hero walking with a ground pet. An air pet gives the bounce nothing to hit.

Scattershot.role: Heavy shots at one target, then fragments spray over the troops behind it. Hits air and ground.
use: Bring your tank in from a different angle, so the spray misses your main army.
Freeze or Overgrowth it as your pack comes into range.
It can't hit closer than 3 tiles, and each shot hits ground or air, never both.
beware: Troops lined up behind a tank. A meat shield does not help, as fragments pass through.
Bowlers, Witches, Hog Riders and Balloons, which all suffer from the spray.

Spell Tower.role: Never attacks. Casts the defender's chosen spell: Rage, Poison, Invisibility or Earthquake.
use: Bait it with a hero, Siege Machine or Skeleton Spell. Reloads are long, so a wasted cast buys time.
Freeze or Overgrowth stops it casting, but not a spell already running. Keep moving through Rage.
Earthquake only hits ground, so air ignores it. Log Launcher logs can set off Invisibility early.
beware: Poison hurts swarms such as Witches and Bowlers. Earthquake takes a share of big ground troops' health.
Killing it is no escape, as a loaded tower still releases its spell when destroyed.

Super Wizard Tower.role: Merged tower. A bolt hits one troop, then chains to many others nearby, air and ground.
use: Keep support troops a few tiles away from your tank, so the chain misses them.
Freeze, Invisibility or Overgrowth stops the bolts. Save one for when your army walks into range.
A Totem Spell draws its fire away from your army.
beware: Clusters and swarms. Hog Riders, Balloons, Witches and Archers all suffer from the chain.
Big flyers still take a heavy first hit, so Dragons feel it too.

Wizard Tower.role: Short range splash that fires quickly at air or ground.
use: Send a tank first, then kill it with Archers, Minions or other ranged troops behind.
Spread out in a line. Never walk a packed swarm into its splash.
Each blast hits ground or air, never both, so Balloons over a targeted Giant are safe.
beware: Clumps of small troops, ground or air, especially Balloons and Minions.

X-Bow.role: Rapid single-target fire with huge reach. Ground only at long range, or air and ground at shorter range.
use: Check the bow. Level means ground only, tilted up means air too. Tactical Overview shows it as well.
A ground-only X-Bow cannot touch air troops, so send them at it.
Put a Golem or Ice Golem in front and swarm it with cheap troops, or Freeze it.
beware: Slow, fragile troops in its long reach, as it locks on early and holds on.

Air Bomb.role: Hidden air trap that blasts everything flying in a small area.
use: Send one Minion or Balloon ahead on your path to set it off.
Spread small flyers out, so one blast cannot catch them all.
Expect them near an exposed Town Hall, storage or Air Defense.
beware: Tight clumps of small flyers. Dragons and other tough flyers can mostly ignore it.
Lava Pups, if it goes off just as a Hound pops.

Bomb.role: Small hidden ground trap that hits everything nearby. Air troops ignore it.
use: Lead with a Giant or other tank, which takes the blast with little harm.
Send one Barbarian ahead of Wall Breakers where walls meet.
beware: Wall Breakers at wall corners, where one blast can kill them.
Stacked Archers or Goblins, and any group standing still to hit a building.

Giant Bomb.role: Big hidden ground trap with a wide blast. Air troops ignore it.
use: Look for empty 2x2 gaps between defences, or a 4x2 gap for a pair of them.
Send one cheap troop through first, and do not drop more near a lit fuse.
Heal survivors straight away. Heroes, Golems and P.E.K.K.A barely notice it.
beware: Groups of small and medium ground troops. A pair can end a Hog Rider attack.
Puppets and other summons dropped before the area is clear.

Giga Bomb.role: Always visible trap with a huge blast and strong knockback, hitting air and ground.
use: Small groups can snipe nearby buildings, as it needs 18 housing close by to go off.
Set it off early with one Yeti or a small group, before your main army comes.
Use Eternal Tome just before the blast. Freeze and Overgrowth do not stop it once armed.
beware: Big packs walking through its zone. Knockback moves even heroes and Golems, and they then retarget.
Do not count on spells to clear it. Lightning, Earthquake, Skeletons and Bats will not set it off.

Seeking Air Mine.role: Hidden mine that chases one flyer and hits it very hard. Small flyers do not set it off.
use: Send a lone Balloon along your path first. Each mine it takes is one less for Dragons.
Or lead with a Lava Hound, which can take the hit.
Minions and Bats are safe from it, so they can follow your tanks without losses.
beware: Dragons, Balloons and Healers pushing on just after an Air Defense falls.
Battle Blimps and a flying Grand Warden, which can lose most of their health at once.

Skeleton Trap.role: Hidden trap that releases Skeletons to distract your troops. It can be set for ground or air.
use: Bring splash. Valkyries, Wizards, Witches and Bowlers clear the Skeletons quickly.
Lightning clears a group near the Town Hall. A Golem's death damage does too.
Keep support behind Giants and Hog Riders, which ignore Skeletons hitting them.
beware: Slow single-target troops such as P.E.K.K.A and Electro Dragons, which waste time on them.
Hero dives near the Town Hall that stop to fight.

Spring Trap.role: Hidden trap that throws the biggest troop it can reach off the map, or hurts it if too big.
use: Be wary of wall gaps and paths. Ground troops walk through them on to the trap.
Send one cheap troop through first. It only takes one troop, so those behind are safe.
That troop must arrive alone, or the trap picks the bigger unit beside it.
beware: Mid-size ground troops such as Hog Riders and Valkyries, which can be removed for good.
Golems and P.E.K.K.A lose health and time. Heroes only take half damage.

Tornado Trap.role: Hidden trap whose vortex holds your troops in place, so defences and other traps can hit them.
use: Send a few cheap troops first, such as Barbarians or Minions, so it fires on them.
Miners and Battle Drills ignore the pull, though they still take its small damage.
Expect it near the Town Hall or core, beside Air Bombs or a Poison Spell Tower.
beware: Packs held under splash. Balloons pulled together are easy work for Air Bombs and Scattershots.
Ground troops pulled on to a wall, which stay stuck until it ends.

glossary.short: A path you clear so your main army walks into the base, not around it.
means: Troops head for the nearest building they want. If outer buildings are left standing on both sides, your army walks off along the edge and runs out of time.
A funnel fixes that. Before the main army goes in, you destroy the buildings on either side of your entry point. What is left in front of the army is the way into the middle.
A poor funnel is one of the most common reasons an attack fails. Heroes, Baby Dragons, Wizards and Siege Machines are the usual funnel makers.
glossary.example: Send a hero down each side to clear the outer buildings, then drop Dragons in the gap between them.

glossary.short: The middle of a base, where the Town Hall and strongest defences usually sit.
means: Most bases keep their most valuable buildings in the centre, wrapped in walls and other buildings. That centre is the core. The defensive core means the same thing, with the focus on the defences in it.
Getting your main damage into the core usually decides an attack. It is why guides tell you to save Rage or Freeze for that moment rather than spend them on the way in.
glossary.example: Rage your Valkyries as they enter the core, where buildings sit close enough for them to hit several at once.

glossary.short: A section of a base closed off by its own ring of walls.
means: Base builders split a base into walled sections. Each one is a compartment. Ground troops have to break in or get lifted over the walls, which costs them time.
It matters because you often want your army inside one particular compartment. That is why you aim Wall Breakers and Jump Spells at a chosen spot rather than at the nearest wall.
glossary.example: Cast a Jump Spell over the wall of the Town Hall compartment, so your Yetis walk straight in.

glossary.short: A tough unit sent first so defences shoot it rather than your damage troops.
means: A tank has lots of health and usually little damage. Its job is to reach the defences first and take the shots while weaker troops behind it do the real work.
Tanky just means hard to kill. Used as a verb, as in Lava Hounds tank for Balloons, it means taking the fire for someone else. A bruiser is a tough troop that also hits hard.
glossary.example: Drop a Golem first. Once the defences are shooting it, send your Wizards behind it.

glossary.short: To make defences shoot one unit so the others get through.
means: Defences can only shoot so many things at once. Anything that draws their fire, or soaks it up, is protecting whatever you send next.
It does not have to be a big tank. Skeletons, a Totem or a Furnace can all waste a defence's shots for a few seconds, and that can be enough.
glossary.example: A Lava Hound sent in first soaks up the Air Defense fire, so your Balloons arrive unhurt.

glossary.short: When a defence picks a target and stays on it.
means: Most defences choose a target and keep shooting it until it dies or moves out of range. That is called locking on. A defence that has locked on to your tank ignores the troops walking past.

This is why order matters. Send the tank first so it gets the attention, then send the damage troops. It also tells you when to spend a spell, as Freeze is best cast the moment an Inferno Tower locks on to your key unit.
glossary.example: Let the Inferno Towers lock on to your Golem before you drop anything fragile.

glossary.short: The route your troops choose by themselves once you drop them.
means: You cannot steer troops directly. Each one walks to the nearest thing it wants to hit, then the next, and so on. Most take any building, but some have a favourite, such as defences, walls or heroes. The route that results is its pathing.

Good attacks are planned around it. You remove buildings or use spells so that the nearest target is always in the direction you want. Overgrowth and Invisibility can steer troops too, because they make buildings something your troops skip.
Air armies care about this as much as ground ones, since a flyer's route decides which defences it passes.
glossary.example: Root a building your army is already hitting with Overgrowth and the whole pack reroutes to the next target.

glossary.short: The main group of troops moving into a base together.
means: The push, or main push, is the group that does most of the work. A ground push is one on foot. Spells and supporting troops are planned around keeping it alive and moving.
A ground core in our tips means the same as a ground push, and has nothing to do with the middle of the base.
glossary.example: Place Healing Spells a little ahead of the main push, so it walks into them.

glossary.short: The unit your attack relies on for most of its damage.
means: Borrowed from other games. The carry is what actually destroys the base, while tanks and support keep it alive. A damage carry and a main carry are the same idea.
Saying a troop cannot carry an attack means it is too weak to win without something else doing the heavy lifting.
glossary.example: In a Root Rider Yeti attack, Super Yetis carry the core once Root Riders have opened the way.

glossary.short: A heavy ground attack that breaks through a base by force.
means: A smash sends a tough, hard hitting ground group through walls and defences together, with a tank in front. It relies on raw power more than on precise spell placement. Yetis, Super Yetis and Root Riders are the usual smash troops.
It works best once a funnel lets the group go in as one, and it suffers against splash damage because the troops stay bunched. The Monolith also hits its high health troops hard.
glossary.example: A Yeti and Super Wizard Smash opens one side with heroes and a Log Launcher, then pours everything through the gap.

glossary.short: Dropping a lot of one troop in a wide line and letting numbers do the work.
means: Spam means less careful placement and more troops. You spread them across a wide front so no single defence can deal with all of them.
It is usually easier to do than a planned attack, but it gives you less control. Our guide contrasts it with controlled ground movement.
glossary.example: Yeti Super Archer Spam: drop a wide line of Yetis, then Super Archers behind them.

glossary.short: An army built almost entirely from one troop.
means: Mass Dragons means nearly all your housing space goes on Dragons. Mass Witches and Mass Hog Riders work the same way.
These armies are often the easiest to learn, because every troop does the same job. They can also be stopped by one thing that beats that troop, such as enough Air Defenses against Dragons.
glossary.example: Mass Dragons is the classic beginner army at TH7.

glossary.short: A hero sent through a base early, kept alive by support, to clear the way.
means: In a hero walk, one hero spends a long time moving through the base at the start of the attack, removing buildings and defences. Healers, Invisibility or other spells keep them alive. The main army comes afterwards through the space they cleared.

Players use walk and charge in two ways. Some say a walk stays near the edge to shape a funnel, and a charge goes deep. Others treat them as the same technique, with a charge just being the bigger job. Expect guides to mix them up, as ours sometimes does.
glossary.example: Walk the Royal Champion with Invisibility down one side, then send Dragons along the path she opened.

glossary.short: A hero sent deep to remove key defences before the main army follows.
means: A charge asks more of the hero than a walk. The hero goes further in and takes out defences that matter, such as an Inferno Tower or Spell Tower, with more spells and support to match.

The army that follows is a separate job. A good charge can still fail if the follow-up is mistimed, and a weak charge leaves that army facing a full base. The word is used loosely, so a walk in one guide may be a charge in another.
glossary.example: Charge the Dragon Duke along one side using Invisibility, then send your air army.

glossary.short: Sending a hero or small group straight into the dangerous part of a base.
means: Diving means going in deep, often alone, to hit something important. It skips the slow work of clearing a route, and the unit is exposed once it gets there.
It only pays off if what it destroys is worth what you might lose. That is why diving heroes often bring a Phoenix or a Spirit Fox, or have a Druid alongside them.
glossary.example: The Royal Champion dives over walls and goes for defences, so staying alive decides how far she gets.

glossary.short: Usually a Queen Charge followed by Hog Riders and Miners.
means: The name comes from mixing two ways of winning. The Queen and her Healers carve out one side and take care of tough defences, and a group of Hog Riders and Miners finishes what is left.
Hybrid can also just mean a mix of two troop types. When our guide says air and hybrid attacks, it means armies that mix air and ground.
glossary.example: Queen Charge Hybrid: the Queen clears one side, then Hog Riders and Miners go in together.

glossary.short: The troops or spells that finish off whatever your main army left behind.
means: Your main army often destroys the core and leaves small buildings around the edge. Those still count towards your percentage and the last star, so something has to reach them before time runs out.
Cheap, fast troops suit this well. Keep a few back rather than dropping them all at the start.
glossary.example: Spread your last Archers around the base to clean up what the Giants did not reach.

glossary.short: Pulling the enemy's Clan Castle troops out so you can kill them away from your army.
means: Enemy Clan Castle troops stay inside until an attacker comes close. A lure is a small troop sent near the castle to bring them out early.
It matters because those troops can wreck a hero or a push that meets them by surprise. Once they are out, you can kill them with a Poison Spell, Lightning, or your own troops.
glossary.example: Send one Giant towards the Clan Castle, then Poison the troops that come out before your Queen arrives.

glossary.short: To take out a single target from a distance, or with little effort.
means: Most often it means killing one chosen building, usually a defence, without fighting through everything around it. It can be done with long range troops, hero equipment or spells. Our guide uses it for removing an Air Defense with Lightning.
Players also use it for a quick cheap attack that grabs one star, such as going straight for an exposed Town Hall.
glossary.example: Snipe an Air Defense with Lightning Spells before your Dragons deploy.

glossary.short: When troops get held up, wasting time and taking damage.
means: A troop stalls when it stops making progress, usually because it is chewing through walls or stuck on buildings that do not matter. While it does that, the defences keep shooting it and the clock keeps running.
It is the problem Wall Breakers, Jump Spells and Overgrowth exist to solve, and often the moment to use a Rage Spell.
glossary.example: Valkyries stall at a wall they cannot get past, so have an entry ready before you send them.

glossary.short: A cheap unit or spell that wastes a defence's attention.
means: A distraction exists to be shot at. It buys your important troops a few seconds or sends a defence in the wrong direction. Unlike a tank, it does not need much health, only good timing.
It works best against single target defences, which can only deal with one thing at a time.
glossary.example: A Skeleton Spell on the Monolith gives it something worthless to shoot.

glossary.short: One side of the base, as seen from where you attack.
means: Attacks are often planned side by side. You might clear the left flank with one hero and the right with another, leaving a clean way into the middle.
A two-flank attack hits two sides at once, so defences have to split their fire. Our guide also says side or shoulders for the same thing.
glossary.example: Drop a Siege Barracks on one flank and a hero on the other to make a funnel.

glossary.short: The ring between a base's outer buildings and its core.
means: Your troops have got past the outside, but have not reached the centre yet. This is often where Air Defenses and other strong defences start reaching them, and where an army can slow down.
Guides mention it when timing a spell, so that it lands as troops enter this part of the base rather than too early or too late.
glossary.example: Cast Haste on Balloons as they push past mid-base, so they do not stall under Air Defenses.

glossary.short: When the attack clock reaches zero before you have finished the base.
means: An attack lasts three minutes once it starts. When the clock reaches zero the attack stops, and you keep only what you have already earned. A time out can cost you the last star even when the army is still alive.
Slow troops are most at risk. So is any plan that spends too long clearing the outside, or a long hero walk that uses up the time your main army needs.
glossary.example: Electro Dragons are very slow, so a long route can run out the clock with buildings still standing.

glossary.short: Flying a Battle Blimp over the base to drop your Clan Castle troops on a target.
means: A Battle Blimp is a Siege Machine that flies towards the Town Hall and releases your Clan Castle troops when it is destroyed or arrives. Used on purpose, it lands strong troops deep in the base early on, where they take out a key defence.
Super Archers are a common load, often with Invisibility or Clone Spells where they land. It is delicate, as Air Defenses and Seeking Air Mines can bring the Blimp down before it gets there.
glossary.example: Fly Super Archers in on a Battle Blimp, then cast Invisibility and Clone where they drop.

glossary.short: Killing a defence outright with spells, usually Lightning and Earthquake, before the army goes in.
means: To zap a defence, you hit it with enough Lightning Spells to destroy it, often adding an Earthquake Spell to save a Lightning. In an army name, it tells you what is being removed so the main troops have an easy run.
Zap Dragons and Zap Lalo clear Air Defenses. Zap Witches clears Inferno Towers. You work out how many spells it takes first, as a defence left on a sliver of health is a wasted zap.
glossary.example: At TH9, Blueprint uses six Lightning Spells and one Earthquake Spell to zap two Air Defenses.

glossary.short: Lava Hounds and Balloons together. Also written Lalo or LavaLoon.
means: The name joins Lava Hound and Balloon. The Lava Hounds go first and tie up the Air Defenses, then the Balloons follow and destroy defences while the Air Defenses are busy.

It is a classic air attack, but it depends on timing. Balloons sent too soon arrive before the Hounds have taken the fire, and sent too late they arrive after the Hounds have died. Zap Lalo removes an Air Defense with Lightning first.
glossary.example: Send Lava Hounds first, then Balloons close behind with Haste and Healing Spells.

glossary.short: An air army mixing Dragons and Dragon Riders, often hitting from two sides.
means: Hydra is used loosely. At its simplest it means Dragon Riders with Dragons or Electro Dragons, so you are not relying on one troop. Many guides also describe it as a two-flank air attack, which makes Air Defenses split their fire.

Our armies called Hydra all mix several air troops, usually with Balloons or a Lava Hound, but differ otherwise. Super Archer Clone Hydra opens with a Battle Blimp, and Dragon Duke Charge Hydra opens with the Duke.
Routes decide it, so plan around where the Air Defenses and Clan Castle sit. It suits bases whose Air Defenses can be split.
glossary.example: Open with a Lava Hound and Balloons on one flank, then send Dragons and Dragon Riders with Rage and Freeze.

glossary.short: A Golem and Hog Rider attack, with Wizards in our version.
means: Go stands for Golems and Ho for Hog Riders. Golems take the fire on one side while Wizards clear a funnel, and then Hog Riders run through the gap to go after defences.
It teaches timing and spell placement, because Hog Riders die quickly if they meet Giant Bombs or splash without healing. Older guides warn that it needs careful scouting.
glossary.example: Heal the Hog Riders at the spot where defences overlap, rather than where they stand now.

glossary.short: Golems in front, Witches behind, winning by steady pressure.
